items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: Sid and I, we grew up -- Sid is a Chicago boy, and he grew up around here, and we were kind of buddy-buddy then... we were very, very close.

ctx.x: You still remind me of Sid Catlett.

Oh, yeah, well, -- but I idolized him so, you know? And then in the years a little later on, it was Chick Webb. I listened to Chick. But Sid and I, we grew up -- Sid is a Chicago boy, and he grew up around here, and we were kind of buddy-buddy then. And that was really one

of the great things about musicians then. You were just like a brother. It didn't matter how much you played, you could hobnob with the greatest guy in the world, and never any inflection of your ability.

items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: And then I worked with Big Sid Catlett and Louis Armstrong's band.

ctx.x: Did any particular drummers fascinate you or influence you?

Yeah, well, really, one of my favorites -- I mean, one of my real favorites was Big Sid Catlett, and I used to be amazed at Big Sid Catlett. This great, big 240 pounds -- or 45 or whatever, six-foot three of whatever he was, big man. And he had a touch on a drum that was phenomenal. It looked like he was playing with feathers. He was just -- and I always admired that in him.
You still remind me of Sid Catlett.
